# acmecorp
**DISCLAIMER:** The content below is generated by Claude and only lightly reviewed for the sake of time.

---

Day-to-day commands and conventions for working in this repo. For the
*why* behind the architecture (module boundaries, tradeoffs, open
questions), see [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](./ARCHITECTURE.md) — this doc assumes that
context and doesn't repeat it.

## Quick start

Before running anything below, your ambient AWS credentials must
already resolve to the `tf-exec` role in the **management** account
(e.g. via an AWS SSO profile) — each `envs/<env>` provider assumes
cross-account from there into that environment's own `tf-exec` role.
See "Accounts and DNS delegation" below for the full picture and the
one-time setup in `bootstrap/`.

```bash
cd envs/staging          # or envs/prod
terraform init
terraform plan            # always review before apply
terraform apply
```

Never run `terraform apply` from `modules/` or the repo root — there's
no state there. State lives per-environment, under `envs/<env>/`.

| Command | When |
|---|---|
| `terraform plan` | Before every apply, no exceptions |
| `terraform apply` | After a plan you've read and understood |
| `terraform fmt -recursive` | Before committing — run from repo root |
| `terraform validate` | Quick syntax/type check, run inside an `envs/<env>` dir |
| `terraform output` | See an environment's outputs (ALB DNS, ECR URLs, role ARNs, etc.) |
| `terraform state list` | See everything Terraform is tracking for that env |

## Naming conventions

Everything follows `acme-<environment>[-<service>]`. If you're
guessing a resource name, guess this pattern first:

| Resource | Pattern | Example (staging) |
|---|---|---|
| ECS cluster | `acme-<env>` | `acme-staging` |
| ECS service / task family / container name | `acme-<env>-<service>` | `acme-staging-api` |
| ECR repository | `acme-<env>-<service>` | `acme-staging-worker` |
| RDS instance | `acme-<env>-db` | `acme-staging-db` |
| ALB | `acme-<env>-alb` | `acme-staging-alb` |
| Public hostname | `<service>.<env>.<domain>` for staging (delegated subdomain), `<service>.<domain>` for prod (bare root) | `api.staging.acmecorp.com` / `api.acmecorp.com` |
| CI deploy IAM role | `acme-<env>-ci-deploy` | `acme-staging-ci-deploy` |
| Account-level `tf-exec` role (one per account: management/production/staging) | flat `tf-exec` — deliberately breaks the `acme-<env>[-service]` pattern since it's account-scoped, not env-scoped | `tf-exec` |

Because the ECS container name and ECR repo name are identical
(`acme-<env>-<service>`), a CI pipeline can derive both from just the
environment and service name later, with no name-mapping table to
maintain. Don't let these drift apart if you rename anything — that
convention is what keeps this cheap.

## Module reference

| Module | What it creates | Key inputs you'll actually touch |
|---|---|---|
| `networking` | VPC, public/private subnets (derived from `vpc_cidr`), NAT, routing | `vpc_cidr` (required, must be unique per env), `az_count` |
| `ecr` | One repo per service | `repo_names` |
| `alb` | ALB, HTTPS listener, ACM cert, host-based routing, Route53 records | `route53_zone_id` (caller creates/owns the zone), `services` (list of name/host_header/port/health_check_path) |
| `rds` | Postgres instance | `instance_class`, `allocated_storage`, `multi_az`, `allowed_security_group_ids` |
| `ecs_service` | One Fargate task def + service (called 3x: api/web/worker) | `image`, `container_port` (null = not behind ALB), `cpu`/`memory`, `environment`, `secrets` |
| `ci_deploy` | GitHub Actions OIDC role for CI deploys | `github_repo`, `passable_role_arns` |

Full variable lists are in each module's `variables.tf` — treat that
file as the source of truth over this table if they ever disagree.

## Accounts and DNS delegation

Three AWS accounts: **management** (Terraform state backend + the
`tf-exec` role you authenticate to day-to-day), **production**, and
**staging**. `envs/prod` and `envs/staging` each assume cross-account
into their own account's `tf-exec` role (`var.tf_exec_role_arn`,
created by `bootstrap/production`/`bootstrap/staging`) — see
`bootstrap/*/main.tf` for the one-time, by-hand setup of all three
accounts, including the AWS Organizations cross-account access needed
to create `tf-exec` in production/staging before it exists there.

DNS is split the same way: `envs/prod` creates and owns the root
Route53 zone (`acmecorp.com`) directly, and `envs/staging` creates and
owns a delegated zone (`staging.acmecorp.com`). Because these are two
independent Terraform states in two separate accounts with no
cross-account provider between them, the parent→child delegation is
wired through a plain variable, not a second provider:

1. `cd envs/staging && terraform apply -target=aws_route53_zone.staging`
   (zone only), then `terraform output staging_zone_name_servers`.
2. Paste those name servers into `envs/prod/terraform.tfvars`'s
   `staging_zone_name_servers`.
3. `cd envs/prod && terraform apply` — creates the NS delegation record
   in prod's root zone, plus everything else.
4. `cd envs/staging && terraform apply` (full) — staging's own ALB
   cert can now validate, since the delegation from step 3 makes
   `staging.acmecorp.com` publicly resolvable.

This is a rare, mostly one-time sequence (only needed on first setup or
if staging's zone is ever recreated) — routine deploys never touch it.
On a brand-new `acmecorp.com` (no prior Route53 zone), you'll also need
to point the domain registrar at the name servers from
`cd envs/prod && terraform apply -target=aws_route53_zone.root`, done
once before step 3 above.

## Common tasks

### Deploy a new image
There is no CI/CD pipeline in this repo yet — deploys are manual
Terraform applies for now (see the [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](./ARCHITECTURE.md)'s limitations section).
Build and push the image yourself, then bump the tag Terraform deploys:
```bash
cd envs/staging
terraform apply -var="api_image_tag=<new-tag>"
```
The `ci_deploy` module already provisions the OIDC-based IAM role a
future pipeline would assume (`acme-<env>-ci-deploy`) — nothing else
here needs to change when that pipeline gets built, only a workflow
file needs to be added that assumes this role.

### Add a 4th service
1. Add its name to `repo_names` in the `ecr` module call.
2. Add an `ecs_service` module block (copy the `worker` block if it's
   not behind the ALB, or the `api`/`web` block if it is).
3. If it's behind the ALB, add an entry to the `alb` module's `services` list.
4. If it needs to reach Postgres, add its security group ID to the
   `rds` module's `allowed_security_group_ids`.
5. If/when a CI pipeline exists, add its build context there too.
6. Repeat in the other environment's `main.tf`.

### Add a new environment (e.g. `dev`)
This section covers a new environment *within an existing account*
(e.g. a second environment sharing staging's account). A genuinely new
*account* needs the fuller `bootstrap/` + DNS delegation dance described
in "Accounts and DNS delegation" above, not just these steps.

1. Copy `envs/staging/` to `envs/dev/`.
2. Update `backend.tf`'s `key` to `dev/terraform.tfstate`.
3. Pick a **new, non-overlapping** `vpc_cidr` — see the CIDR scheme
   note below.
4. Update `local.name` to `acme-dev` in `main.tf`.
5. `cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars` and fill in real values.
6. `terraform apply` creates `acme-dev-ci-deploy` via the `ci_deploy`
   module automatically — whenever a CI pipeline exists, that's the
   role it should assume for this environment.

**VPC CIDR scheme** — second octet = environment, so ranges never
collide if these VPCs are ever peered or connected via Transit Gateway:
`staging` = `10.0.0.0/16`, `prod` = `10.1.0.0/16`, next new env = `10.2.0.0/16`,
incrementing from there. Subnet CIDRs are derived automatically by the
`networking` module — you only ever set `vpc_cidr`.

### Rotate the DB password
Nothing to do in Terraform — RDS manages the master password automatically
(`manage_master_user_password = true`) and rotates it via Secrets Manager.
To force an out-of-cycle rotation:
```bash
aws secretsmanager rotate-secret --secret-id <arn-from-terraform-output-db_master_user_secret_arn>
```
ECS tasks read the current value at container start, so a rotation
alone won't propagate to running tasks — redeploy the `api` and
`worker` services afterward. `terraform apply` with no other changes
won't restart them; force it directly:
```bash
aws ecs update-service --cluster acme-<env> --service acme-<env>-api --force-new-deployment
aws ecs update-service --cluster acme-<env> --service acme-<env>-worker --force-new-deployment
```

### View application logs
```bash
aws logs tail /ecs/acme-<env>-<service> --follow
```
Log group names always match the ECS service name (`ecs_service`
module creates one log group per service, retention configurable via
`log_retention_days`, default 30 days).

### Get a shell in a running task (no SSH exists — this is the replacement)
```bash
aws ecs execute-command \
  --cluster acme-<env> \
  --task <task-id> \
  --container acme-<env>-<service> \
  --interactive \
  --command "/bin/sh"
```
Get `<task-id>` from `aws ecs list-tasks --cluster acme-<env> --service-name acme-<env>-<service>`.
Note: ECS Exec isn't enabled on the service by default in the current
module — add `enable_execute_command = true` to the `aws_ecs_service`
resource in `ecs_service/main.tf` if you need this regularly.

### Change task sizing (cpu/memory) or replica count
Edit the relevant `ecs_service` module block's `cpu`, `memory`, or
`desired_count` in the environment's `main.tf`, then `plan`/`apply`.
Valid Fargate cpu/memory combinations are fixed by AWS — check the
[Fargate task size table](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task-cpu-memory-error.html)
before picking new values, invalid pairs fail at apply time.

### Tear down an entire environment
```bash
cd envs/<env>
terraform destroy
```
This will refuse if `deletion_protection = true` on the RDS instance
(prod default) — that's intentional. Set it to `false`, apply, *then*
destroy, if you really mean to delete a protected environment's database.

## Secrets reference

| Secret | Where it lives | How Terraform references it |
|---|---|---|
| DB master password | Auto-created by RDS in Secrets Manager | `module.rds.master_user_secret_arn` output, wired into `ecs_service.secrets` |
| SMS/email provider API key | Created by hand once (see [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](./ARCHITECTURE.md)) | Passed in via `sms_email_provider_secret_arn` tfvar |
| CI deploy role | No secret — OIDC, no long-lived credentials | `ci_deploy_role_arn` output goes into a GitHub repo secret (the *ARN*, not a credential) |

Nothing above should ever appear as a literal value in `.tf` files,
`terraform.tfvars` (only `.tfvars.example` is committed), or a PR diff.
If you see a real secret value in a diff, stop and rotate it.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| `terraform apply` fails creating `ecs_service` on first-ever apply | ECR repo has no image yet — push one before the service can start (see [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](./ARCHITECTURE.md)) |
| ECS service stuck at 0/1 running tasks | Check `aws logs tail /ecs/acme-<env>-<service>` first; usually a bad image, missing env var, or the task can't reach Secrets Manager/RDS (check security groups) |
| ALB health checks failing | Confirm `health_check_path` in the `alb` module's `services` list actually returns 200-399 on that service, and that the service's security group allows ingress from the ALB's SG on `container_port` |
| A future CI pipeline fails at `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` | GitHub OIDC provider missing from the account, wrong `github_repo` value in `ci_deploy`, or the branch/ref doesn't match the trust policy condition |
| `terraform plan` wants to replace the VPC | Someone changed `vpc_cidr` after the VPC already existed — this is a destructive change, don't apply without a migration plan |
| Two environments have overlapping CIDRs | Check `vpc_cidr` inputs — this repo's convention is one `/16` per environment, second octet = environment; see the CIDR scheme note above |
| `terraform plan`/`apply` fails with an `AssumeRole` / access-denied error | `var.tf_exec_role_arn` is missing or wrong in that env's tfvars, or management's `tf-exec` role hasn't been granted `sts:AssumeRole` on that account yet (check `bootstrap/management`'s policy) — see "Accounts and DNS delegation" |
| ACM certificate validation hangs / never completes | The parent zone's NS delegation record for that env's zone isn't live yet (or the registrar isn't pointed at the root zone's name servers) — follow the ordering in "Accounts and DNS delegation" instead of a plain full `apply` |
